A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CLoQ research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete Appendix A are readable and matchable despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-modeling, arithmetic-reasoning and commonsense-reasoning experiments, together with quantization and initialization ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds model evaluations, ApiQ comparisons, sensitivity experiments and initialization-resource measurements.

M1.justification: The MagR/OPTQ quantization, activation-weighted objective, two-SVD initialization and adapter fine-tuning remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 now explicitly includes Gram-matrix regularization already described in v1. The new pseudoinverse discussion concerns theoretical solutions rather than a changed experimental procedure.

E1.justification: The represented datasets and tasks remain WikiText-2, GSM8K/Math10K, the four arithmetic benchmarks and eight commonsense benchmarks. The mixed-training experiment recombines already represented math and commonsense data. Additional model families, calibration counts and sequence lengths change experimental settings within this coverage.

E2.justification: ApiQ was discussed but not evaluated in v1. v2 adds ApiQ-lw and ApiQ-bw to the Llama2 WikiText/GSM8K comparison and ApiQ-bw to arithmetic and commonsense comparisons. These substantial additions introduce a closely related competing initialization method while retaining the previous comparators.

E3.justification: v2 adds Llama3-8B and Mistral-7B configurations, mixed Math10K-plus-5K-commonsense training, calibration-size sweeps from 32 to 256, and fine-tuning sequence lengths from 256 to 2048. It also evaluates initialization duration and peak GPU memory. Existing default settings, splits and Appendix A hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses of mixed-domain training, calibration-size sensitivity, sequence-length sensitivity and initialization efficiency (Tables 6 and 8–10). It removes v1's group-size analyses (Tables 4–5) and the Hadamard initialization variant from the adapter-factorization ablation. The remaining factorization comparisons are retained.

E5.justification: v1 provides no repeated-run counts or uncertainty estimates. v2 Table 4 reports CLoQ's Llama3 arithmetic accuracies averaged over five random runs with standard deviations. This reporting is limited to that configuration; no increased run count is established for retained experiments.

E6.justification: Shared Llama2 entries in v1 Tables 1–3 remain numerically unchanged in v2 Tables 3, 1 and 5. Substantial results are added for ApiQ, additional models and new analyses, while group-size and Hadamard results disappear. New Table 4 reports arithmetic averages of 59.0±0.34 for CLoQ versus 57.4 for ApiQ-bw. Table 5 also exposes exceptions to superiority: 4-bit Llama2-7B commonsense averages favor ApiQ-bw, 84.7 versus 84.2.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.1 and its proof remain unchanged. v2 adds a mathematical discussion extending the optimality condition to rank-deficient activations and supplies a pseudoinverse-based solution, supplementing the original full-rank treatment.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement and conclusion retain the same central claims: calibrated, gradient-free initialization, closed-form optimal adapters and strong low-bit fine-tuning performance. Specifying 2-bit in the abstract and clarifying that initialization is gradient-free refine wording without materially redefining the contributions.

C2.justification: v2 newly interprets calibration-size stability as supporting practical deployment and explains comparable LoftQ initialization time through fewer SVDs balanced against costlier quantization. It also develops resource-efficiency implications from measured costs. The earlier interpretation of robustness across quantization group sizes is removed.

D1.justification: Table 10 newly documents initialization time and peak GPU memory, including CLoQ's 0.7 hours/9 GB for Llama2-7B and 1.5 hours/13 GB for Llama2-13B. v2 also describes LoftQ's five default alternating iterations. Code access and existing implementation details remain unchanged; Appendix A still provides hyperparameters only for Llama2.

R1.justification: v2 adds contextual references including PiSSA, OLoRA, RoseLoRA, Eckart–Young, Llama3 and additional quantization and initialization research. It supplements the computational comparison with LoftQ, while retaining the principal positioning against LoftQ, LQ-LoRA and ApiQ.

P1.justification: Most introductory, methodological, concluding and appendix prose is retained. v2 revises result discussions around ApiQ, adds experimental discussion blocks, introduces the AltMin abbreviation and updates author and acknowledgment text. The overall section organization remains largely stable.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the predominantly two-column layout with a single-column journal format and substantially reformats the title block, equations and tables. Comparison tables are expanded and reordered, new experimental tables are added, and group-size tables are removed. Figures 1–2 retain identical image content.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important evidential gaps by evaluating the closely related ApiQ baseline, testing additional model families and measuring previously unquantified initialization costs. Sensitivity experiments further strengthen the method's empirical support. These gains outweigh the loss of group-size and Hadamard ablations, although reporting remains imperfect: Table 4 supports a 1.6-point Llama3 arithmetic advantage over ApiQ-bw, whereas the prose claims 2.1 points. Overall, the central effectiveness and efficiency claims have substantially stronger direct evidence.
